title: Youth.Heritage.Europe. brings youth voices to third Policy Debate on responsible tourism and heritage
content:
How can cultural tourism support heritage conservation without placing additional pressure on the places and communities it celebrates? This question guided Youth.Heritage.Europe.’s third Youth Policy Debate, organised within the frame of the EU-funded European Heritage Hub.

With welcoming remarks from Jasna Popović, Secretary of Youth.Heritage.Europe, and a panel moderated by Sophia Dibbs, Youth.Heritage.Europe.’s Programmes Officer, the event on 30 September 2026 brought together Chiara Ronchini, Theo Alexandridis, Daphne Gerodimou, and Andrea Bringas to discuss responsible tourism and the role of young people in shaping heritage practices.

The discussion explored the tensions between attracting visitors, protecting heritage, and maintaining the quality of life of local residents. Theo Alexandridis, one of the Hub’s NextGen Heritage Ambassadors, outlined environmental deterioration, physical damage, and social displacement associated with overtourism. Examples from Barcelona, Venice, Amsterdam, and Dubrovnik illustrated how destinations are responding through visitor management and restrictions on cruise tourism.
